prompt: A deeply emotional, cinematic, and slightly surreal wide-angle photograph of a dimly lit, dusty room. Dominating the entire background wall is a massive, oppressive, antique mechanical clock face with no numbers, just heavy iron hands. Sitting on the floor in the foreground, arranged neatly from left to right, are five young people of increasing age: a 2-year-old toddler, a 5-year-old, a 9-year-old, a 14-year-old, and an 18-year-old. Each is staring intently into a glowing tablet or laptop. From the back of each device, physical umbilical-like cables stretch back and plug directly into the center of the giant clock. The thickness of these cables drastically increases from left to right: the toddler is connected by a single, fragile, thin wire. The middle children have progressively thicker, heavier cords. On the far right, the teenager is completely slumped over, physically burdened and crushed by a massive, overwhelmingly thick bundle of heavy, parasitic industrial cables that are stretched tight, visibly dragging the iron hands of the giant clock downward. Dramatic, moody chiaroscuro lighting, no text anywhere, no numbers, pure visual metaphor.
dataset_name: Common Sense Census: Media Use by Tweens and Teens
insight: As children grow, screen time evolves from a lightweight, temporary distraction into a heavy, inescapable tether that drains the overwhelming majority of their waking hours.
